spec.name: Reversal v33
spec.notes: Mean reversion of recent returns across names. Adds the vendor's revised sentiment score.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 3.2, annual return 12%, maximum drawdown 4%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 3.23 to -2.86 (change -6.09). The strategy already trades a bar after its signal, so this measures how fast the signal fades, not look-ahead.
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 3.23 to 0.79. Changed by strict mode: fields sentiment_revised.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 2.63 (as submitted, 8 bps: 3.23); it breaks even at 18.7 bps with daily turnover 0.45.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 3.23 against 3.23 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is -0.79 against 3.23 in research, a gap of +4.02.
The best year gives 26% of total P&L (year 8) and calm regimes give 2%; Sharpe is 2.99 in calm and 4.16 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.42, so the claimed 3.20 becomes 2.78 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 5.66 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.05, 95th percentile 0.44).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 3.23 to as low as 1.61 (as low as 2.40 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 72% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 53% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

exhibits.summary: The scan (a heuristic) found no phrase addressed to reviewers or giving instructions in 2 text sources.

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (pit_replay EX-2, holdout_test EX-5).
